tweets.text:
There’s still so much opportunity in the diffusion of AI into the real world. Most enterprises are going to need a ton of support to be able to apply the model breakthroughs to their workflows.

Intelligence alone is not enough to transform most processes because you need to bridge that intelligence with real world feedback loops. That requires connecting to various enterprise systems, getting the right data to the AI, enabling humans to make decisions at different steps in a process through the right UX, having workflows that improve the underlying data and models over time, dealing with regulatory and compliance challenges, and more. 

The way you implement AI agents for doing client onboarding in a bank is entirely different from contract review in a legal team. In life sciences, financial services, legal, manufacturing, and many other critical industries, AI is only valuable if it makes contact with the real world in a contextual way. 

The way that interaction is going to happen is through an applied AI layer. Some of that will come from the labs directly, but lots of the opportunity will necessarily come from independent companies that can go deep in each industry.

And counter to some beliefs, this need isn’t reduced even as AI model capability improves over time. In fact, the better the models get, the more ambitious you can be in the workflows you can automate, which generally requires even more of this applied layer. Tons of opportunity right now.

Very happy to have Box sign this letter. We’re big believers in the power of open weights AI.

Open weights models help to drive the industry forward in a variety of ways to ensure more innovation, creativity, and diffusion of AI.

You get to have layers of the stack that emerge to post train models for highly specific purposes, which makes AI more useful in real world scenarios. Instead of waiting for just a few players to go deep in a domain, you get dozens or hundreds of attempts at that vertical, like in finance, life sciences, legal, healthcare, and more.

You get to see variance in how to handle safety and cyber risks. Instead of just one approach, you get a peek into what happens advanced capabilities can be used to build better systems to are used to defend systems. 

You get alternative approaches to training and building AI models. In more compute constrained environments, you develop more novel and efficient approaches to model training, which every other lab can learn from. 

And you get different cost structures for different workloads. High end and orchestration tasks can go to the closed frontier models and specific workhorse tasks can be done more cheaply. 

Open vs. closed is not a zero sum battle. The reason why you want strong open weights models is because it pushes the entire AI industry forward.

tweets.text:
BREAKING: Claude Opus 5 is OUT NOW!

And…it’s a hard model to love.

We’ve spent the last week @every testing it across coding, writing, knowledge work, and our internal agent.

It argued with instructions, stopped before the work was finished, and generally didn’t play well with our existing skills and plugins like Compound Engineering. Our first reaction was: What have they done to my boy?

Then we deleted our existing skills and started from scratch.

Without the elaborate workflows we had built for earlier models, Opus 5 got dramatically better, and even showed flashes of brilliance.

Here’s our Day 0 vibe check:

- It’s a poor man’s Fable. It has many of Fable’s personality quirks without Fable’s genius.
- It breaks backward compatibility. If you’re using it with existing skills and workflows, watch out. It will often stop early or otherwise miss your instructions.
- If you start from scratch, you’ll have better results. @KieranKlaassen figured out that if he just started from scratch without his existing skills, he could get dramatically better results. This is a model that takes some time to rebuild your workflows around—but if you do, there’s a payoff waiting.
- Medium or low effort works better. @KieranKlassenn also found better results using Opus 5 on lower thinking levels. It seems that the more time you give it to think, the more likely it is to do the more annoying behaviors. Don’t just switch to Sonnet for a faster response! Try low thinking.

I have two slots in my workflow:

Chatted with a friend who leads security at a public company following the GPT Sol incident. some interesting takeaways.. 

How do you manage security for effectively infinite agents when identity and access management was designed for a finite number of employees?

One employee can now spin up hundreds of agents. Those agents can spawn more agents.

Traditionally, each employee has an identity, a role, permissions, and a lifecycle.

Do agents inherit the spawning employee’s permissions? What’s their lifecycle - a task, a ticket, a week? Do child agents inherit the same permissions? How do you audit all of this?

The best way to think about AI is as a force multiplier for the fields you already know about (or for the rate at which you want to learn about a new one). The 3rd category -no existing judgment, no interest in developing it- will basically produce slop and won’t drive that much economically productive activity.

Because they can wield these tools in ways that actually drive high quality output, veer agents in the right direction when they go off, and actually incorporate the work into something useful.

The expert engineer with agents will do far more productive work, precisely because they know how to steer the agent properly. The designer will product far better outcomes using AI than someone without an eye for design. And so on.

As a result of this dynamic, specialization will continue to be important, if not even more so as the tools get more powerful. Because the expectation of the market gets to be much higher. Getting good at any craft will continue to be necessary in the future.

tweets.text:
Very good post from the Head of Economics at Anthropic. They’re finding that jobs have been less negatively impacted by AI than expected, as we continue to see time and time again in the data.

The reason for this is that AI - at least so far - still requires people to operate to produce value in most cases. Most jobs can’t be fully automated with AI, only certain tasks in those jobs. And when you automate specific tasks, you actually can get even more output from those jobs, raising the demand (or at least maintaining it) in many cases.

“So far, AI is both skill-biased and labor-augmenting. It complements domain expertise. It relies on humans in the loop to direct and evaluate the most complex work. And it rewards AI proficiency. Model capabilities are improving fast, but remain stubbornly jagged. To fill in the pockets of the jagged frontier, expert oversight is needed to steer incredibly capable AI systems, and to recover when they falter.”

I suspect that we continue to see this in a number of critical areas of work. It’s clearly happening in software engineering, where software produced is being multiplied, all of which still requires developers to manage the work agents are doing. Software engineers are needed in a wide variety of industries now and companies of all sizes can now light up software projects that would have been impractical before.

But there will be plenty of other domains of work where demand remains strong in a world where agents can accelerate the output of that job. Jevons paradox is alive and well.
tweets.summary_zh: 这篇文章提到，AI 对工作的影响没有想象中那么大。虽然AI技术在不断进步，但大部分工作还是需要人来操作，AI只能帮助完成一些任务，而无法完全取代人类。因此，AI实际上可能会让工作效率更高，从而增加对某些职位的需求。比如，在软件工程领域，虽然AI能提高生产力，开发者仍然是必不可少的。而且，随着AI的应用，其他行业的工作需求也会继续保持强劲。

tweets.text: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10 minutes, total mess, anything goes, full stream of consciousness. Sometimes I declare it up top, something like "switching to speech recognition sorry for any typos...". Sometimes I turn it into a small interview of a few turns. But I find that the LLMs are somehow very good at reconstructing long incoherent rambles and often their echo of your own tangle of thoughts comes out quite a bit cleaner than what you started with. The result is that you improve the mind meld and have to correct things less from that point on.

very notable trajectory comparison writeup here buried in the RLM paper from @a1zhang and @lateinteraction.

an open secret of "frontier" model training is that even without training on test, you can basically cheat by training on test lookalikes, enabling you to goalseek almost any benchmark number you want.

however when they are released open weights, 99% of the time the norm is that you do not get the datasets/rlenvs that would easily show you if someone was training on Temu Tbench, so there is plausible deniability. Alex and Omar discuss applying standard NLP distance metrics on hidden trajectories. There's no ultimate solution here, but they have some prelim explorations. It happens to support the finding that RLMs can generalize to unseen tasks that share latent structure observed in training.
tweets.summary_zh: 这篇文章讨论了一个关于“前沿”模型（指最新、最先进的AI模型）训练的有趣现象。即使不直接在测试数据上训练，开发者也能通过训练与测试数据相似的数据来获取好的成绩，这算是一种“作弊”。不过，当这些模型的代码和数据发布后，大部分情况下我们无法看到实际使用的数据集，这样就有了“可否认性”（意味着很难证明有人真的作弊）。文中还提到了一些关于如何用标准的自然语言处理（NLP）技术来分析这些模型在训练时的表现。虽然还没有完美的解决方案，但他们已初步探讨了一些方法。总的来说，这些研究支持了这样的发现：这些模型可以适应新的任务，只要这些任务与它们训练时的模式有相似之处。

tweets.text:
Multi-model agentic systems clearly are the future. Great post by cursor. Their new research shows that a frontier model as a planner and orchestrator with a workhorse cheaper model can materially lower the cost of total tokens on a project, resulting in a 15X cost improvement.

“Few moments in a large task genuinely require frontier intelligence, such as the original decomposition, the design decisions, and certain trade-offs. Once a frontier planner has collapsed the ambiguity into a detailed, explicit instruction, less expensive models simply have to follow it.”

This is increasingly becoming the core design pattern of complex agents, because the tokens used on large amounts of work on many tasks don’t require the same intelligence threshold as the planning step. By routing to different models based on where you are in the task, you get much greater efficiency overall. 

This provides the template for where the applied layer in AI will differentiate. You can only drive this efficiency if you know the domain well and have the ability to work with multiple model tiers; companies that can do this will across coding, finance, legal, healthcare, life sciences, and other critical spaces will be in a strong position to get larger workloads that would otherwise be too expensive for the customer to deploy.

podcasts.title: How Supabase Became One Of The Fastest Growing DevTool Companies In The World
podcasts.summary_zh:
视频讲述了Supabase如何迅速崛起为全球增长最快的开发工具公司之一。通过分享其发展历程、商业策略及核心产品，视频深入探讨了这家公司如何利用开源技术和社区支持来吸引开发者，并在竞争激烈的市场中脱颖而出。

🎯 推荐 Yves 观看 — 该视频提供了关于开发工具行业的宝贵见解，对Logic Labs以及TexTale在AI工具和电商运营中的应用有很大启发。

podcasts.name: Greg Isenberg
podcasts.title: Naval says calendars are dumb (LIVE Q&A)
podcasts.summary_zh:
这个视频讨论了Naval Ravikant对传统日历的看法，认为日历有其局限性，并提到如何用更有效的方式管理时间和专注力。通过公开问答的形式，Naval分享了他对时间管理、效率和创造力的见解，从而引导人们更加高效地利用时间。

🎯 推荐 Yves 观看 — 该视频探讨了高效时间管理对于创意工作的重要性，能够帮助Logic Labs和TexTale更好地提升团队的工作效率和创造力。

podcasts.name: Y Combinator
podcasts.title: Compute at Sea
podcasts.summary_zh:
这段视频讨论了在海上进行计算的潜力和技术挑战，尤其是在推进海洋环境中的数据处理和AI应用方面。它介绍了如何利用海洋环境作为计算资源，提供了对未来技术发展的展望，特别是在气候变化和资源管理的背景下。

🎯 推荐 Yves 观看 — 该视频涉及到在新环境中应用AI和技术的创新思路，这与Logic Labs和TexTale在电商和创意设计中的应用有直接关联，值得关注。

podcasts.name: TBPN
podcasts.title: AI Agents Hack Hugging Face, White House Promotes Science’s Golden Age | Diet TBPN
podcasts.summary_zh:
本视频探讨了 AI 代理如何突破 Hugging Face 的技术限制，以及白宫对科学黄金时代的推动，展示了 AI 在推动科技进步和政策支持方面的重要作用。内容涵盖了 AI 的实际应用以及当前的行业动态。

🎯 推荐 Yves 观看 — 这个视频涉及 AI 代理和 Hugging Face 的技术创新，与 Logic Labs 在 AI 产品开发上的工作密切相关，并且对创意设计的应用具备启发性。

podcasts.name: Y Combinator
podcasts.title: Multiplayer AI
podcasts.summary_zh:
这段视频讨论了多人AI系统的开发和应用，如何通过协作增强AI的智能表现，以及这种技术如何在各个领域带来革命性的变化。它展示了不同的应用案例，帮助观众理解多人AI的潜力和未来发展方向。

🎯 推荐 Yves 观看 — 这个视频涉及AI在产品开发中的应用，可能会为Logic Labs的项目提供启发，同时在创意设计方面也可以引发新的思考。

producthunt.name: Acti
producthunt.tagline: Agentic keyboard for mobile commands and search
producthunt.summary_zh: Acti是一款专为移动设备设计的智能键盘，能够快速输入命令和进行搜索。它简化了用户在手机上执行操作的过程，提高了效率。用户可以通过触击键盘，轻松调用各种功能和信息。

producthunt.name: Context.dev
producthunt.tagline: One API to scrape, enrich, and extract the internet
producthunt.summary_zh: Context.dev 是一个API工具，能够从互联网上抓取、丰富和提取数据。用户可以通过它轻松获取网站上的信息，并将这些数据进行整理和分析。它适用于各种数据集成和自动化需求。

producthunt.name: Pazi
producthunt.summary_zh: Pazi 是一款专注于业务运营的工具，通过“Vibe code”技术帮助企业高效管理和优化日常流程。用户可以使用它进行数据分析、流程自动化和团队协作，提高工作效率和决策能力。

producthunt.name: OpenSEO
producthunt.summary_zh: OpenSEO 是一个开源的 SEO 工具，旨在提供与 Ahrefs 相似的功能。用户可以通过它进行关键词研究、网站分析和竞争对手跟踪，帮助提升网站的搜索引擎排名。无需付费订阅，适合希望自主管理 SEO 的用户。

producthunt.name: AnySearch
producthunt.tagline: Real-time structured search trusted by agents and developers
producthunt.summary_zh: AnySearch是一款实时的结构化搜索工具，专为代理和开发者设计。它能快速整理和提供准确的信息，让用户能够高效地找到所需的数据和答案。通过直观的界面，AnySearch简化了搜索过程，提高了工作效率。

producthunt.name: ExploreYC
producthunt.tagline: Open-source API for Y Combinator & a16z company data
producthunt.summary_zh: ExploreYC 是一个开源API，提供Y Combinator和a16z公司的数据。用户可以通过这个API获取相关公司的信息、融资情况和其他关键数据，方便进行研究和分析。

producthunt.name: ClawTeams
producthunt.tagline: The first goal-driven, proactive AI team for e-commerce
producthunt.summary_zh: ClawTeams是一款专为电商设计的主动式AI团队，旨在帮助商家实现目标。它能分析市场趋势、优化运营策略，并自动执行促销活动，提高销售效率。通过智能化管理，ClawTeams简化了电商运营流程。

producthunt.name: Paradigm
producthunt.tagline: Turn any goal into a personalized, adaptive learning path.
producthunt.summary_zh: Paradigm是一款智能学习平台，能够根据用户的目标创建个性化和灵活的学习路径。用户只需输入自己的学习目标，系统便会推荐适合的学习资源和步骤，帮助用户高效达成目标。

producthunt.name: Fuzzy AI
producthunt.tagline: We warm your prospects before reaching out
producthunt.summary_zh: Fuzzy AI 是一款智能营销工具，旨在通过人工智能技术分析潜在客户的兴趣和行为。在你联系他们之前，Fuzzy AI 可以自动为你预热这些客户，提高成交的可能性。它让营销更加高效，节省时间和精力。

producthunt.name: Fypro
producthunt.tagline: Convert your TikTok followers into paying customers
producthunt.summary_zh: Fypro 是一款工具，可以帮助用户将 TikTok 上的粉丝转化为付费客户。它提供数据分析和营销功能，使用户能够有效地推广产品和服务，从而实现收益增长。

producthunt.name: Glaze by Raycast
producthunt.tagline: Create your own Mac apps by chatting with AI
producthunt.summary_zh: Glaze by Raycast 是一款让用户通过与人工智能对话来创建自己的 Mac 应用程序的工具。用户只需简单输入想法，AI 就能快速生成应用的代码和功能，让开发变得更加轻松。这个产品降低了编程门槛，适合任何想要自定义应用的人。

producthunt.name: Sim
producthunt.tagline: Open-source workspace for AI agents and workflows
producthunt.summary_zh: Sim 是一个开源的平台，专为人工智能代理和工作流程设计。用户可以在这个平台上创建、管理和协作各种 AI 任务，提高工作效率。它支持自定义和扩展，适合不同的工作需求。

producthunt.name: Unabyss for Claude
producthunt.tagline: Shared memory across all apps and LLMs. In Claude
producthunt.summary_zh: Unabyss for Claude是一个用在Claude平台上的工具，它允许用户在多个应用和大型语言模型（LLMs）之间共享记忆。通过这个产品，用户可以更高效地保存和访问信息，实现跨应用的数据同步。

producthunt.name: Cursor for iOS
producthunt.tagline: Build with coding agents from anywhere
producthunt.summary_zh: Cursor for iOS 是一款移动应用，允许用户通过编程代理在任何地方编写和管理代码。它提供了一个直观的界面，方便用户进行代码编辑、调试和项目管理。无论你是新手还是有经验的开发者，都可以在此平台上轻松工作。

producthunt.name: Lev8
producthunt.tagline: Find, research, and reach the right people
producthunt.summary_zh: Lev8是一款帮助用户寻找和联系合适人选的工具。它允许用户进行深入的研究，以便更好地了解目标群体并与之建立联系。通过Lev8，用户可以简化信息获取和沟通的过程。

github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个基于蓝牙网状网络的聊天应用，允许用户在没有互联网的情况下进行聊天，类似于传统的IRC聊天。对于Yves来说，这个项目可以帮助TexTale在无网络环境下实现客户间的即时沟通，提升用户体验；同时也为Logic Labs提供灵感，以便他们在AI与社交应用结合方面进行创新。
Amnezia VPN Client 是一款用于保护用户在线隐私和安全的虚拟专用网络（VPN）工具，支持桌面和移动设备。对于 Yves 来说，这个项目可能对 TexTale（科技服装电商）有帮助，因为增强的网络安全可以保护客户的个人信息，提升购物体验，同时也有助于维护品牌形象。作为创意设计从业者，了解和应用这样的安全工具也能帮助他在设计过程中更好地保护创意作品和商业秘密。

github_trending.description: 💖🧸 Self hosted, you-owned Grok Companion, a container of souls of waifu, cyber livings to bring them into our worlds, wishing to achieve Neuro-sama's altitude. Capable of realtime voice chat, Minecraft, Factorio playing. Web / macOS / Windows supported.
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个自托管的虚拟助手，可以进行实时语音聊天并在游戏中互动，类似于拥有一个数字角色伙伴。对于Yves来说，这个项目可能对Logic Labs（AI公司）更具价值，因为它展示了如何将人工智能应用于互动体验，能为创意设计提供新的灵感和方向，同时也可以探索在电商环境中虚拟角色的潜力。

github_trending.description: A lightweight, cloud-native GIS platform for visualizing, exploring, and analyzing geospatial data. It runs in the web browser, on the desktop, on mobile, and inside Jupyter notebooks.
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个轻量级的地理信息系统平台，可以帮助用户在浏览器、桌面和手机上可视化、探索和分析地理数据。对于Yves来说，它可能对Logic Labs（AI公司）更有帮助，因为这个平台可以应用于地理数据分析，支持与AI相关的创意项目和研究。同时，这种工具也能助力于提升品牌营销策略，尤其是在地理定位方面。

github_trending.description: Pretty fancy and modern terminal file manager
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个现代化的终端文件管理器，旨在提供一个美观且高效的文件操作体验。对于Yves来说，它可以帮助Logic Labs在处理大量数据文件时提高工作效率，同时也能在TexTale的电商平台上更好地管理和组织产品及设计素材，提升创意设计的流畅性。

github_trending.description: 小红书笔记 | 评论爬虫、抖音视频 | 评论爬虫、快手视频 | 评论爬虫、B 站视频 ｜ 评论爬虫、微博帖子 ｜ 评论爬虫、百度贴吧帖子 ｜ 百度贴吧评论回复爬虫 | 知乎问答文章｜评论爬虫
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个爬虫工具，可以自动获取多个社交媒体平台（如小红书、抖音、B 站等）上的用户评论和帖子内容。对于Yves来说，这个工具可以帮助TexTale收集用户反馈和市场趋势，进而提升品牌营销策略；同时，也能为Logic Labs提供丰富的社交数据，助力AI模型的训练和优化。作为一名创意设计从业者，Yves可以利用这些数据洞察用户需求，从而激发创意灵感。

github_trending.description: The design language that makes your AI harness better at design.
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个设计语言工具，旨在帮助用户更好地将人工智能应用于设计，从而提高设计质量。对Yves的Logic Labs（AI 公司）特别有帮助，因为它可以提升AI在创意设计中的表现，使得最终产品更加吸引人，符合市场需求。同时，这也能间接促进TexTale（科技服装电商）的品牌形象和用户体验。

github_trending.description: Kronos: A Foundation Model for the Language of Financial Markets
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目Kronos是一个针对金融市场语言的基础模型，旨在帮助用户更好地理解和处理与金融相关的数据和文本信息。对于Yves的Logic Labs，这个项目能够提供强大的AI能力，助力开发更加智能的金融分析工具；而对于他在TexTale的电商业务，虽然不直接相关，但可以启发如何将复杂数据转化为有价值的洞察，支持市场营销决策。作为创意设计从业者，Kronos也可以激发他在金融主题产品或服务方面的创意设计灵感。

github_trending.description: Open-source & free — Battle-tested at Alibaba's scale. Hybrid architecture code review tool: deterministic pipelines + LLM Agent, precise line-level comments, built-in fine-tuned ruleset (NPE, thread-safety, XSS, SQL injection), OpenAI & Anthropic compatible.
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个开源的代码审查工具，能够在大型工程中高效地检查和评估代码质量，确保安全性和性能，使用了先进的 AI 技术。对Yves来说，这个工具可以帮助Logic Labs提升其AI产品的代码质量，并为TexTale在开发技术服装电商平台时，确保代码的安全与高效，从而提升整体业务的稳定性和用户体验。作为创意设计从业者，使用这样的工具可以让他更专注于创意工作，而将代码审核的细节交给智能化的解决方案。

Jenkins 是一个自动化服务器，可以帮助开发者帮助在软件开发过程中实现持续集成和持续交付，也就是自动化构建和测试代码。对于 Yves 来说，Jenkins 可以在 Logic Labs 中提高 AI 项目的开发效率，确保快速迭代和高质量输出，或者在 TexTale 的电商平台中优化网站和应用的发布流程，确保用户体验的持续提升。此外，作为创意设计从业者，Jenkins 也能帮助他更好地管理和部署与设计相关的工具和项目。
